bibliographic.title: Developing a Data-Driven Player Ranking in Soccer Using Predictive Model Weights
bibliographic.venue: Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD '16)

scope.rationale: Introduces Pass Shot Value (PSV) and Average Pass Shot Value (APSV), an early data-driven framework for valuing passes based on their association with shot opportunities, using model weights from a supervised shot-prediction classifier. Directly relevant to the action-valuation / pass-value lineage in the SAVANT corpus.

model.name: Pass Shot Value (PSV) / Average Pass Shot Value (APSV)
inputs: possession-level aggregation (average of per-pass feature vectors)
model.target: Binary outcome of a possession: whether the possession (>= 3 completed passes) ends in a shot taken by the offensive team (y in {1, -1}).
model.architecture: L2-regularized linear Support Vector Machine (LIBLINEAR) with asymmetric (class-specific) cost parameters; per-pass value PSV(i,j) = w_i^o + w_j^d + w_ij^od derived from learned model weights.
model.spatial_resolution: 18-zone pitch grid (3 rows x 6 columns) with continuous closeness-weighted representation to the N=2 nearest zones

data.provider: unspecified hand-labeled event-data vendor (Opta is referenced contextually but not stated as the source)

evaluation.splits: Chronological game-level split: first 80% of games as training, final 20% as holdout; 5-fold cross-validation on the training set with folds constructed at the game level so possessions in a single game are not split across folds.

claims.statement: The shot-prediction model has an AUROC of 0.79 and an F-score of 0.31 on the holdout set.
6 of the top 10 most influential features for predicting whether a possession ends in a shot involve zone 14 (the 'critical zone' centered in the field in front of the penalty box).
Zone 17 (directly in front of the opposing team's goal) does not appear among the top 10 features.
Passes to zone 14 from zone 5 or zone 9 (long completed passes into zone 14) have negative model weights, while the top two features overall are passes between corner areas and zone 14.
Among players in the 'offense' category, APSV correlates significantly with goals scored over the season (rho = 0.27, p < 0.05), even though goals and assists are not used in computing APSV.
APSV is computed only over players with more than 200 completed passes in the 2012-13 La Liga season, and only over passes occurring in possessions of 3 or more completed passes.

APSV is almost always negative because most possessions do not end in a shot; offensive players like Cristian Tello, Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and the midfielder Mesut Ozil have a positive APSV.
The 18-zone field representation uses a continuous closeness-weighted vector r^l of length 18 with N=2 non-zero entries, normalized so that the L1-norm sums to 1.

Each pass is converted into a feature vector of length 360 (18 origin features + 18 destination features + 324 flattened origin-destination outer-product features); a possession's feature vector is the average over its completed passes.
On average, each La Liga team attempted around 18,000 passes during the entire 2012-13 season; Barcelona made the most (30,283) and Levante the fewest (13,094).

limitations: The analysis does not incorporate temporal information such as duration of possession or time elapsed between passes; the authors note that adding such information would provide more situation-specific insights.
The work uses only event data; the authors state that player-tracking data would better allow investigation into strategic aspects of the game not directly involving the ball.

Features do not capture sequential information within a possession; the authors note that expanding to sequential features could give a more detailed understanding of how passing strategy relates to outcomes.

The model is trained on a single team-agnostic dataset; the authors note that team-specific models built from a team's own event data could provide better analysis of strategies most promising in their system.
open_questions: Extend the framework to defensive actions: use actions taken by players on defense to predict defensive outcomes and rank players by defensive ability.
Incorporate temporal information (e.g. duration of possession, time elapsed between passes) into the analysis.
Utilize player-tracking data as the source dataset to study off-ball strategic aspects of play.
Expand features to include sequential information within a possession.
Build team-specific models from individual teams' event-data collections.
Extend the methodology to other sports such as basketball, where passing performance is also primarily measured by assists.
